FY2026 year-end leverage of 2.1x (pre-IFRS16 EBITDA ~A$510m) implies net bank debt ~A$1,070m, ~A$50m LOWER than the Dec-2025 figure used here -- conservative by ~A$0.25/share; refresh when the FY2026 annual report is in the folder.

inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built, single rate for all three scenarios (owner-fcf.md s7f: risk lives in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into per-scenario rates -- the prior DCF's 9.0/8.5/10.5 charged it twice). Cost of equity: AU 10-yr govt ~4.3% + 5.0% ERP x beta 1.0 (the stock fell 33% in a year against a flat market and carries 2.1x ND/EBITDA; a 0.85 defensive-distributor beta no longer fits the observed volatility) = 9.3%. After-tax cost of debt: FY2025 borrowing costs A$89m on ~A$1.1bn = ~8.1% pre-tax, 5.8% after 28.5% tax. Market weights E 74% / D 26% (mkt cap A$3.44bn, net debt A$1.18bn) -> 8.4%, rounded to 8.5%. Prior model used 9.0% base.
inputs.model_currency_note: currency=AUD is the ISO code of the statements; quote_currency=NZD is the ISO code of the NZX price.
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company, non-US, cyclical-lite healthcare distributor -> owner-fcf.md incl. section 7). Same family as the 2026-06-27 DCF, but rebuilt from components on a 10-year horizon because the margin is still ramping; the prior file grew reported (levered) FCF at scenario rates. UPDATE of the 2026-06-27 DCF -- see reconciliation.

FY0 = FY2026 actuals from the 19-Aug-2026 result (revenue A$13,481m, underlying EBITDA A$614m, underlying FCF A$241m, reported FCF A$204m, leverage 2.1x). The FY2026 annual report is NOT in Extracted/ (CSV ends at H1 FY2026), so balance-sheet anchors are 31-Dec-2025.

LEASES: treatment (B) -- leases as operating cost. Lease cash (principal + interest; FY2025 A$80.7m = 0.66% of revenue, H1 FY2026 A$44.1m = 0.65%) is charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct 0.65%; lease liabilities (A$473.9m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A (0.68%) is ex-ROU (FY2025: PPE depreciation ~A$33m + amortisation A$46.7m; H1 FY2026 18.6 + 25.2 annualised). The prior DCF charged NEITHER (reported FCF excludes lease principal, and its net debt was bank-only) -- that overstated value by ~A$60m/yr of lease principal.

UNLEVERED: interest on borrowings (A$113.5m paid FY2025, ~A$120m FY2026) is not deducted from the flows because net bank debt is subtracted in the bridge; the prior model deducted it from FCF AND subtracted net debt (the interest double-count).

EBITDA margin driver is on the UNDERLYING post-IFRS16 basis (FY2026 4.55%; FY2027 guide A$635-655m), with lease cash then deducted explicitly. Statutory EBITDA was lower by DC transition/M&A one-offs (~A$20-30m/yr in FY2025-26) that end with the program; PPA amortisation (~A$20m/yr, non-cash, non-deductible) is inside the 0.68% D&A and the tax rate is set at 28.5% (guided ETR ~28%) to absorb the lost deductibility.

WORKING CAPITAL: distributor -- NWC ~5.5% of revenue (~20 cash-conversion days), but FY2026 absorbed only A$7m on +A$1.2bn revenue and FY2025 released A$75m on the CW exit. Modelled as a 3% capture on the CHANGE in revenue (base), 2.5% bull, 4% bear -- an OUTFLOW when revenue grows.

CAPEX: FY2026 ~A$145m (final DC year) -> FY2027 guided ~A$100m (0.71% of revenue) -> 0.70% thereafter, approximately equal to ex-ROU D&A. Pre-program FY2021-22 capex was 0.3% of revenue, so 0.7% is not a low bar.
NCI: charged once, via the A$57.9m put-option liability in the bridge; NCI profit share (~A$3m/yr, <1.5% of NPAT) is left in the flows as immaterial.

ASSOCIATES / OTHER FINANCIAL ASSETS: income from associates (A$15m FY2025) stays inside EBITDA and the A$55.9m investment is therefore NOT added to the bridge; A$25.9m of other financial assets (equity instruments at FVOCI) earn nothing in the flows and are omitted from the bridge for conservatism (~A$0.13/share).
M&A: ~A$121m of FY2026 bolt-ons (Paringa, K-Talyst, etc.) and the ~A$150m FY2027 capacity are NOT modelled; FY2027 guidance also excludes them. Any accretive deal is upside to every scenario.

PRICE DISCREPANCY: EBO.NZ_Analysis.json (2026-09-08) cites a price of NZ$29-30 and a 52-week high of NZ$41.98; Yahoo's NZX and ASX quotes and the 12-month bar history (52w 19.00-30.88, high in Sep-2025) do not support that, and EBO.AX x AUDNZD ties to NZ$20.48 within 0.2%. The analysis's price commentary appears to be a year stale; the valuation uses NZ$20.48.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 underlying EBITDA guidance midpoint (A$645m, +5.0% on A$614m) sitting inside the revenue CAGR band (3yr 4.5% / 5yr 7.0% to FY2025; 3.3% / 7.9% to FY2026). Equity CAGR (12.6%/15.9%) is inflated by the FY2025 A$250m placement and M&A goodwill; EPS CAGR (-1.4%/+1.7%) is depressed by the FY2024 Chemist Warehouse loss and peak DC D&A; neither describes forward earnings power.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (+12.6%) diverges from EPS 3yr CAGR (-1.4%) by more than 30pp. Cause: A$254m of new equity (FY2025 placement + retail offer + DRP) and acquisition goodwill grew book value while the Chemist Warehouse Australia contract loss (~A$1.9bn revenue, FY2024) and the DC renewal program's D&A/interest step-up compressed EPS. Book-value growth is not earnings growth here; the model is anchored to guidance, not to either CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - IFRS-16 lease principal - SBC, per year from the cash-flow statements (FY2026 from the 19-Aug-2026 result: reported FCF A$204m, lease principal ~A$61m est. from H1 x2). Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR 6.9% vs reported 7.4%: lease principal grew from A$32m (FY2020) to A$57-69m as the DC network moved onto leased sites, so ~0.5pp/yr of reported FCF growth was paid for in lease commitments. This series is LEVERED (post-interest); the forward model is unlevered, so the two are not directly comparable.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands inside the A$635-655m guide (modelled A$647m on +5.5% revenue and a 4.55% margin). The DC program is complete, so capex steps down to the guided ~A$100m (0.71% of revenue) and stays near 0.7% -- roughly equal to ex-ROU D&A -- while Kemps Creek productivity, the July-2026 expanded CSO regime, and faster-growing Retail Pharmacy Brands / MedTech / Animal Care lift the group EBITDA margin from 4.55% to a 4.9% plateau by FY2032 (still below the ~5.0% of FY2021-22, because 1PWA caps and GLP-1/high-value-medicine mix keep compressing GOR margin). Revenue growth decays from 5.5% to 3% as GLP-1 volume growth normalises. Working capital absorbs 3% of each year's revenue increase (~20 cash-conversion days). Terminal value hits the 15x owner-FCF cap; Gordon at 8.5%/2.5% would have paid 17.1x.
scenario_narratives.bull: GLP-1 and >A$1,000/dose medicines keep compounding at double digits, Retail Pharmacy Brands (780+ stores, retail media, CareClinics) and MedTech/aesthetics (K-Talyst, Origin Biologics) grow well ahead of group, and Paringa/SVS lift Animal Care -- revenue +7% in FY2027 tapering to 3.5%. FY2027 EBITDA beats the top of the guide (modelled A$666m) and the DC automation payback (30% Kemps Creek uplift) plus mix shift carries the margin to 5.4% by FY2034. Working-capital drag is lighter (2.5% capture) as cash-conversion days keep improving. Terminal growth 3.0%. This needs BOTH the growth and the margin legs to come through; ~A$150m/yr of self-funded bolt-ons are NOT in the numbers and are upside to this case.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2027 productivity inflection slips: FY2027 EBITDA misses the guide (modelled A$604m, a repeat of the April-2026 fuel-driven downgrade), the New Zealand Chemist Warehouse wholesale contract rolls off at end-CY2026 (management-sized at ~1% of group EBITDA, ~A$6-8m, ~2% of revenue at wholesale margins -- charged as -1.5% revenue growth and -0.15pp of margin in FY2028), and GOR margin compression from 1PWA caps and GLP-1 mix does not reverse, leaving the margin at 4.2-4.3% through the horizon. Post-commissioning IT/optimisation spend keeps capex at 0.75% of revenue and working capital absorbs 4% of revenue growth. Revenue growth 1.5-3%. Terminal growth 2.0%. Leverage stays near the top of the 1.7-2.3x range but there is no going-concern or covenant path here -- the bear is a low-return, no-re-rating distributor, not a solvency case.

valuation.currency_note: All monetary values in AUD millions; per-share values in NZD (unsuffixed, quote currency) and AUD (_aud twin) at AUD/NZD 1.231. street_* = SBC treated as non-cash (memo).

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the base-scenario interim owner FCF and exiting at year 10 returns a 15% IRR. Terminal value is rebuilt AT THE HURDLE (min(Gordon@15%, 15x FCF_10)), per the 2026-09-01 correction; the prior DCF's NZ$17.71 was TV-per-share discounted at 15% on the WACC-built Gordon value, which the spec has since retired.
entry_price.note: A hurdle entry price well below intrinsic value is the expected shape for a 3-5% grower discounted at 8.5%: demanding 15% from an asset whose cash flows the model discounts at 8.5% costs roughly that. The current NZ$20.48 implies a 10.5% IRR on the base path (terminal value rebuilt at that rate; see required_return_table).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_10)). The 8.5% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Base-case driver paths; WACC rows x terminal-growth columns; terminal value = min(Gordon, 15x FCF_10) at each cell, so low-WACC/high-g cells are cap-bound and flatten. Values in NZD at AUD/NZD 1.231.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 (unchanged from the 2026-06-27 DCF) rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear held at 25% because the FY2027 margin/cash inflection is still unproven in a clean annual print, GOR margin compression has not yet turned, and the NZ Chemist Warehouse roll-off is the second contract loss to the same counterparty in three years; there is no solvency or covenant path, which is why it is not higher. Bull cut to 25% because it needs both a growth leg (7% revenue) and a margin leg (5.4%) to come through with no M&A credit.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is ~0.05% of revenue, so house and street differ by only ~NZ$0.7/share; the price sits BELOW the house (fully-SBC-expensed) value, so band position is negative and the SBC regime is irrelevant to the gap. Near-degenerate but not null: SBC is small, not zero.

prior_version.model: 5-yr growth on reported (levered) FY2025 FCF A$293.4m, Gordon-only terminal, per-scenario WACC 9.0/8.5/10.5, net bank debt 1,120.9, 205.0m shares, AUD/NZD 1.10

bridge.item: Prior weighted IV (2026-06-27, price NZ$20.65, AUD/NZD 1.10)

Flows rebuilt: unlevered component build from FY2026 actuals (EBITDA 614 -> FY27 guide 645), lease cash charged in the flows (treatment B), interest no longer deducted from FCF, FY27 capex ~A$100m -- on the prior 5-yr Gordon frame and prior WACCs
Horizon 5 -> 10 years and terminal value capped at 15x owner FCF (Gordon exceeded the cap in every scenario)
Single 8.5% AUD WACC in all scenarios (prior 9.0/8.5/10.5 charged risk in both the flows and the rate)
Anchors: diluted shares 205.0 -> 206.3m, NCI put liability A$57.9m added to the net-debt bridge

reconciliation.bridge_note: Bridge is on the probability-weighted value; steps are sequential (each measured with all earlier steps applied). NZD column converts each AUD step at the PRIOR rate 1.10 and takes the FX move last on the fully-rebuilt AUD value. Price moved NZ$20.65 -> 20.48 (-0.8%), so upside changed almost entirely through the IV, not the price.
unchanged_deliberately: Probability weights 25/50/25 -- would move on a clean FY2027 print (bear down) or a third Chemist Warehouse-type loss / another guidance cut (bear up).
Terminal growth 2.5/3.0/2.0 -- would move on a structural PBS/CSO reform or a change in ANZ healthcare spend trajectory.
Lease treatment is NEW (the prior file charged neither principal nor liabilities); the FY2025-26 lease cash run-rate (0.65% of revenue) is what would move it.
Dividend/DRP policy is not modelled -- the DRP dilutes ~1%/yr for cash; refresh the count from the FY2026 annual report.
driver_changes_vs_prior: Y1 is now FY2027 (prior Y1 was FY2026, now actual: EBITDA A$614m vs the prior file's A$615m assumption -- delivered). FY2027 EBITDA anchored to the A$635-655m guide (base A$647m) and capex to the ~A$100m guide, both now confirmed rather than promised.
Bear case now carries the NZ Chemist Warehouse roll-off as a specific FY2028 hit (-1.5pp revenue, -0.15pp margin) instead of generic 'additional contract losses'.

FY2025's reported FCF A$293.4m (prior base) is no longer the anchor: it embedded a ~A$75m one-off CW working-capital release; FY2026 underlying A$241m / reported A$204m is the starting point, rebuilt unlevered from components.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

valuation_philosophy.primary_method: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF: 10-year explicit component build (EBITDA margin - SBC - lease cash - D&A - tax on EBIT + D&A - capex - working-capital build), terminal value = min(Gordon, 15x FCF_10), discounted at a single 8.5% AUD WACC, net bank debt + NCI put deducted, three probability-weighted scenarios (25/50/25).
valuation_philosophy.fcf_definition: Owner FCF is unlevered and after ALL lease cash (IFRS-16 principal and interest) and a 0.05%-of-revenue SBC charge; it is NOT the company's 'underlying free cash flow' (which is post-interest, pre-lease-principal and excludes one-offs).
valuation_philosophy.currency_handling: DCF entirely in AUD (reporting currency). Per-share values converted to NZD at AUD/NZD 1.231 (Yahoo AUDNZD=X 2026-09-08), parity-checked against EBO.AX. Unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are NZD; *_aud twins are the model currency.
valuation_philosophy.key_driver: Whether the completed A$360m DC program converts into margin: the base case needs 4.55% -> 4.9% over six years while capex settles at ~0.7% of revenue. Each 0.1pp of EBITDA margin across the whole path is worth ~NZ$1.04/share; +0.5pp of WACC costs ~NZ$1.22/share (9.0% row of required_return_table vs 8.5%).
limitations: FY2026 balance sheet not yet in the folder: net debt and share count are 31-Dec-2025 (net debt conservative by ~A$50m vs the 2.1x leverage disclosed for 30-Jun-2026; count ~2-4m light for 2026 DRP issuance).
FY2026 actuals (revenue, EBITDA, FCF) are taken from the result release as summarised in the Analysis JSON, not from an extracted filing.
AUD/NZD at a 12-month extreme (1.231); a reversion to 1.15 would cut NZD values ~6.6%.
Bolt-on M&A (~A$121m FY2026, ~A$150m FY2027 capacity) is excluded, as is any sum-of-parts premium for the TerryWhite Chemmart network, DC real estate or MedTech intangibles.
Analysis JSON's price commentary (NZ$29-30, 52w high NZ$41.98) is inconsistent with Yahoo NZX/ASX quotes and was overridden by the live NZ$20.48.

methodology.engine_contract: assumptions[scenario] carries growth_rates, ebitda_margin_path, sbc_pct_path, lease_cost_pct, da_pct, capex_pct_path, wc_capture_pct, cash_tax_rate_path, wacc, terminal_growth, terminal_cap_multiple, horizon_years; projections[scenario].revenue[0] / (1+g1) recovers the FY2026 base of A$13,481m; the dashboard derives the NZD/AUD rate from intrinsic_value / intrinsic_value_aud.
